articleTitle: Deep learning techniques for the study of student's academic performance during distance education caused by COVID-19
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: In this work, we study the influence of various educational factors on the academic performance of school students during the transition to distance learning format due to the COVID-19. The coronavirus pandemic affected not only health system, but also all aspects of human lives, including educational system as well. The study is based on a large dataset consisting of school students marks for 2020 academic year taken from “Electronic education in Tatarstan Republic” system's database. The data analysis and interpretations were performed by using modern deep learning methods (feed-forward neural networks) and feature importance detection techniques by using Captum framework. This method allows us not only to obtain features with the most significant impact on the prediction, but also introduces numerical characteristics for its quantitative evaluation and comparison. The studied educational factors include teachers' characteristics, mean marks for pre-pandemic period, number of grades, group of school subject and school characteristics. As a result, we discovered that the most significant feature is the mean mark for pre-COVID19 period, thus, general trend of school marks remained pretty similar to that period, but not identical. Also, we established importance on pupil's changes of marks a certain schools and types of schools, teachers with certain age and gender that can be explained by different period of adaptation to the rapidly changing situation.

articleTitle: Comparison of Time Series Databases
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: Time series data is data that contain a series of timestamps and special values. Plenty of industrial areas generate time series and are used for the monitoring system. The amount of collected data and operational analysis required a new type of database: Time Series Databases, which are specialized for storing and querying time series data. In this paper, we propose a list of popular time series databases and a feature list of open-source databases. The search resulted in 4 databases. Therefore, five criteria are defined: speed of writing and reading, size of the database, support time-series table, and convenience of API.

articleTitle: Attrition Rate Measuring In Human Resource Analytics Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: Nowadays, the majority of educational institutions try to improve the working conditions (job satisfaction, salary, workload, and work-life balance) of their employees so that they remain in their institutions for a long time. However, often in the same institutions, the number of resignations remains at about the same level. In such cases, it is important to identify the trends of such employees and prevent further resignations. This work aims to use Machine Learning (ML) algorithms for predicting the probable quitting of employees to help Human Resources (HR) henceforth retain valuable employees in advance, thereby benefiting both employees and the institution as a whole.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an IoT-based Smart Pillbox for Improving Medical Adherence
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: The absence of timely and proper intake of medicines can pose great health hazards for patients and elderly persons suffering from critical illnesses. An IoT-based smart pillbox is being proposed to overcome that problem. This pillbox aims to help the patients take the correct medicines at scheduled times in the right amount and also to help keep track of the medical history of the patient. The pillbox can be set up using an app and then it will alert the patient using a buzzer at scheduled times and upon pushing the button after taking particular medicine from the specified drawer, it will update the medicine intake information in the cloud server so that the caregiver can get notified about any unwanted exceptions. It will also keep the count of pills and provide a reminder when the pill count gets low. Thus this smart pillbox aims to ease the life of patients and maintain the well-being of their health.

articleTitle: Fake News Classification using BLSTM with Glove Embedding
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: Considering the extensive utilization of social media platforms, false information is more likely to spread rapidly among users. With the surge of user-generated content, a significant amount of the information being shared is in-accurate and has no connection to reality. It can be chal-lenging to automatically identify and verify the accuracy of textual content. This research project aims to employ B-LSTM deep learning model with dynamic and static pre-trained embeddings to classify news datasets utilizing three fake news benchmarking datasets.

articleTitle: A Matrix Factorization-based Collaborative Filtering Framework for Course Recommendations in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: In higher education, students are often faced with a plethora of elective courses, making it challenging to determine which courses align with their academic and career goals. Recommender systems offer a potential solution to this problem by utilizing data on students' past academic performance, interests, and goals to provide personalized course recommendations. This paper proposes a personalized course recommendation system based on collaborative filtering with matrix factorization. The proposed method analyzes data from 603 students and provides third-year course recommendations for each student based on their individual preferences and past academic performance. The system has the potential to assist students in selecting the most appropriate elective courses, improving their academic performance, and enhancing their overall educational experience.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Stochastic Dynamic Vehicle Routing Problem
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: In this study, we propose solving the Stochastic Dynamic Vehicle Routing Problem with Deep Reinforcement Learning. We propose a fully attention-based model consisting of a dynamic encoder and decoder to learn the routing policy of a single vehicle, where the customer orders appear over time. To train the model, we utilize a reinforcement learning setting, in which a reward signal guides an agent to select nodes to be visited. The computational analyses demonstrate the suggested strategy's superiority over the chosen benchmark algorithms.

articleTitle: Automatic Language Identification from Audio Signals using LSTM-RNN
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: The objective of this study is to develop an efficient Language Identification (LID) system using Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Networks applied to audio signals. Two experiments were conducted to validate the proposed approach. The experimental results demonstrated exceptional performance, with an accuracy of 98% and 97.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on the test sets of the first and second experiments, respectively. The models were trained and tested using audio recordings in English, Russian, Turkish, Kyrgyz, and Kazakh languages. These findings suggest that the proposed LID system is highly effective and can be used in various real-world applications.

articleTitle: Recommendation System for Human Resource Management by the Use of Apache Spark Cluster
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: In this paper, there has been built and tested recommendation systems for recommending new positions for employees on Apache Spark by the use of a cluster of physical servers. The cluster has been built in the university, and the code has been executed both on a cluster, google colab, and a standalone mode. It was shown that the current cluster spends more time on the execution in comparison with colab, but as new servers get added to the cluster and the size of dataset is to increase, the performance will be much faster in comparison with colab. It can be valuable in HR departments which wish to use their own servers for the security purposes.

articleTitle: Machine Learning as an effective tool for Human Resource management in recruiting process in the higher educational field
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: In the era of advanced technology and digitalization, the use of machine learning makes it possible to increase the efficiency of the recruitment process. This study aims to identify various variables that directly play a role in recruitment. The study also addresses the HR sphere problems and proposes a solution related to the use of machine learning. The research methodology includes an analysis of the characteristics which are dominated by past candidates. The data obtained suggests that machine learning can bring significant benefits to the recruitment process, such as reducing the cost and time for selection, reducing emotional factors, and increasing accuracy. Overall, this study provides valuable insight into the potential of machine learning in recruitment and highlights how it can be used to facilitate the recruitment process.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in Crowd Analysis: A Survey of Current Research Trends
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: Deep learning, or artificial neural networks, has been used for years to solve a range of problems. The computation burden increased with the intricacy of challenges and models as well as with the volume of data. This research provides a quick overview of the process of moving beyond artificial neural networks to deep learning, theories, and applications. There's also information regarding used libraries, applications, or electronics. Specifically covered the canonical strategies for crowd analysis. Throughout the study on deep learning approaches for a crowd, analysis is included in the literature as well as an overview of datasets. Studies carried out more recently have also been reviewed and compared. As a result, crowd analysis is an area of inquiry that blends academic theory with real-world application. As a corollary, deep learning is utilized to achieve successful outcomes in the academic and practical realms of crowd analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Self-esteem on Students' Performance in Online Programming Competition
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This paper will look at the effect of self-esteem on students' performance in online programming competitions. The competition was conducted in a hackerrank platform with 4 rounds in total. On each round, there was a set of general questions such as age, gender, etc., but also self-esteem related questions to evaluate how much self-esteem a person has. Correlation between self-esteem and results of each round on average was calculated. The average obtained correlation was around -0.11. Based on the results, the conclusion was that the correlation is slightly low and negative which claims that too high self-esteem can result in low results in online programming competitions across students.

articleTitle: Designing User Experience (UX) for Special Education: Principles, Practices, and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: For educators, families, and education providers, the enrollment and education of pupils with disabilities in the general education classroom have been challenging and polarizing. The trend of enrolling disabled students in general and specialized education classes will continue, and educators are looking for teaching strategies that enhance inclusion. With a growing emphasis on inclusive education, it is important to ensure that learners with disabilities or special needs have equal access to educational resources and opportunities. However, designing UX for special education presents unique challenges that must be addressed to create a positive and effective learning experience for all learners. The purpose of this paper is to address the above concerns and give helpful strategies for inclusive education by using “User-sensitive inclusive design” that is flexible enough to accommodate a greater spectrum of pupils and fulfill their educational needs regardless of their mental health. The importance of user-sensitive, inclusive design in special education is highlighted and provides insights and recommendations for designina effective and inclusive UX for all learners.

articleTitle: Free products of operads and Gröbner base of some operads
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit definition of the free product of operads and present a method for determining its basis and dimension. We demonstrate the application of these tools to well-known operads that have two operations. Additionally, we provide examples of operads that are isomorphic to the free product of operads that arise from commutators and anti-commutators. Namely, these operads are Lie-admissible, associative admissible, and metabelian-admissible. Furthermore, we introduce an operad that generalizes the Leibniz operad and prove that an anti-commutative operad can be embedded into this operad via a commutator. We also construct a basis for this operad.

articleTitle: HIVA: Holographic Intellectual Voice Assistant
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: Holographic Intellectual Voice Assistant (HIVA) aims to facilitate human computer interaction using audiovisual effects and 3D avatar. HIVA provides complete information about the university, including requests of various nature: admission, study issues, fees, departments, university structure and history, canteen, human resources, library, student life and events, information about the country and the city, etc. There are other ways for receiving the data listed above: the university's official website and other supporting apps, HEI (Higher Education Institution) official social media, directly asking the HEI staff, and other channels. However, HIVA provides the unique experience of “face-to-face” interaction with an animated 3D mascot, helping to get a sense of ‘real-life’ communication. The system includes many sub-modules and connects a family of applications such as mobile applications, Telegram chatbot, suggestion categorization, and entertainment services. The Voice assistant uses Russian language NLP models and tools, which are pipelined for the best user experience.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Open-Source Educational Robot for Hands-On Learning Experiences in IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: The use of educational robots has increased rapidly over the past few years due to the growing interest in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) education. In this paper, we introduce an open-source and open-design educational robot for practicing Internet of Things (IoT) using hands-on experiences. The robot is equipped with various sensors and actuators, and is controlled by an Arduino microcontroller. We describe the design and implementation of the robot, including the hardware and software components. The hardware design consists of a wood cut by laser cutting machine, which houses the Arduino microcontroller, sensors, and actuators, as well as the wheels and motor drivers for movement. The software is based on an Arduino IDE and Blockly, where each sensor and actuator can be programmed on C programming language, and can be easily added or removed. The capabilities of the robot are demonstrated through several experiments, such as obstacle avoidance, line following, and temperature monitoring. The robot can serve as an effective tool for teaching students the fundamentals of IoT, robotics, and programming, as well as encouraging creativity and innovation in STEM education. The potential applications of the robot in various computer science courses are also discussed as further work.

articleTitle: Time Series Models for Predicting Data Traffic Values: Topic: Wireless and mobile sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This article has considered a variety of uncomplicated time-series models for the purpose of making predictions. Forecasting network traffic has been an area of significant interest, particularly for network congestion monitoring, data flow control, and network management. By carefully selecting a traffic model, the most crucial features of network traffic, including short--term and long-term dependent processes and self-similarity over extended time periods, have been able to be identified and predicted. The article has explored forecasting methods such as Holt's model and the second-order polynomial model.

articleTitle: Model of a two-dimensional free boundary problem in an cylindrical shape electrical contact
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: A method for the numerical solution of an axisymmetric problem in a model that describes the change in temperature and coordinates of the free boundary in a cylindrical contact is considered. The mathematical model consists of an inhomogeneous heat equation with variable coefficients and an additional differential equation for the kinetics of phase changing, but there is no differential equation for a free boundary in it. This is the main difference from Stefan's free-boundary approach, where solving 2-3-dimensional problems is very difficult. The method was used earlier to solve a one-dimensional problem and a satisfactory agreement with the solution of the corresponding Stefan problem was obtained.

articleTitle: Research of the parameters of a solar battery of composition materials for spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: Solar batteries are one of the most reliable, modern and well-tested options for providing spacecraft with energy. The growth of solar cell efficiency allows to increase the power capacity of the spacecraft (SC). In the course of the study, the main aim was achieved: a 3D model of a solar battery for a spacecraft was created in the SolidWorks program, a static analysis and modeling of the model in SolidWorks Simulation were carried out. The results obtained during the research make a certain contribution to the study of solar batteries, increasing the efficiency of their use in outer space. Modern methods for studying the parameters of a solar battery made of a composite material for spacecraft were used when performing the study.

articleTitle: Investigating The Factors That Influence Kazakh Female Students' Interest In STEM Careers Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: The underrepresentation of women in STEM fields is a global problem that demands urgent attention, and Kazakhstan is no exception. Despite efforts to close the gender gap in STEM education, only 32% of undergraduate students in Kazakhstan's STEM programs are female, indicating that more needs to be done to address this issue. To tackle this problem, a groundbreaking study was conducted using machine learning techniques to analyze a dataset of female high school students in Kazakhstan. The innovative use of machine learning allowed the researchers to extract patterns and identify the most influential factors that shape Kazakh female students' interest in STEM careers. This is a step forward in the field, as the use of machine learning to address this issue is rare. The study's findings highlighted the importance of self-efficacy, parental support, and the availability of role models in STEM fields as key factors that influence Kazakh female high school students' interest in STEM careers. Based on these findings, programs that focus on increasing self-efficacy, parental involvement and support, and exposure to successful STEM professionals and role models can be implemented to encourage more female students to pursue STEM careers.

articleTitle: Kazakh Handwritten Text Recognition Using Computer Vision and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to digitizing handwritten text in the Kazakh language. Despite the numerous methods available to recognize handwritten characters, such as Convolution Neural Networks, Recurrent Neural Networks, and Connection Temporal Classification algorithms, these approaches have not been entirely successful in recognizing Kazakh script. Our investigation into the limitations of these existing methods reveals that visual feature extraction alone is insufficient for accurately recognizing Kazakh handwritten text. As a result, we developed a Kazakh Handwritten Text Recognizer (HTR) that combines the strengths of each method. Our experimental results demonstrate that our approach improves the recognition accuracy of Kazakh handwritten text. This paper presents a promising solution for digitizing handwritten Kazakh text and paves the way for further research in this area.

articleTitle: MBTI-based recommendation system for extracurricular activities for high school students
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This paper proposes MBTI-based recommendation system for extracurricular activities for high school students. The system extracts personality types from student profiles using feature engineering and utilizes machine learning algorithms to recommend relevant extracurricular activities. We evaluate the system's performance using precision, recall, and F1-score metrics and compare it with other state-of-the-art recommendation systems. Our results show that the MBTI-based recommendation system outperforms other systems and provides a more personalized approach to activity selection. We also discuss the potential impact and benefits of the system for high school students and identify areas for future research. Overall, this paper contributes to the growing body of literature on recommendation systems and highlights the importance of considering personality types in the recommendation process.

articleTitle: Overview of Deep Learning Models for Banknote Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This paper offers a comparative analysis of various deep learning models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and Deep Belief Networks (DBNs), applied to the task of banknote recognition. Accurate banknote recognition is indispensable in financial transactions, vending machines, and security systems, and the development of reliable recognition systems is essential to mitigate fraud and ensure seamless operation. In this study, we employed the Banknote dataset, containing a balanced mixture of genuine and forged banknotes, to train and test these models. Our ex-perimental results demonstrate that the CNN model, specifically with ResNet-50 architecture, outperforms the others in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score. The paper encapsulates the performance metrics and considerations for applying these models to banknote recognition, and aims to assist researchers and practitioners in choosing the most effective methods for future development of banknote recognition systems.

articleTitle: Forecasting the Probability of a Power Outage Using Binary Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This paper considers the use of machine learning methods to forecast the probability of a power outage at a substation. The data on power outages for 2 years were analyzed. They contained information about the substation where the emergency power outage occurred and information about the weather. A solution is proposed for forecasting the probability of a power outage caused by weather factors. The features for compiling training and test samples are determined, an analysis is carried out to select the appropriate algorithm for training the model. A model was trained for further use in forecasting the probability of outages.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of the Analysis of PM2.5 Sources in Kyrgyzstan with 31 Selected Countries
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the impact of population density, CO2 emissions, and tree coverage on air quality in Kyrgyzstan by analyzing it with 31 other countries. The study em-ploys three types of analysis: correlation, mapping, and seasonal analysis. The correlation analysis revealed that population density has a medium effect on air quality index (AQI), with a correlation coefficient of 0.43. Tree coverage has a negative correlation of -0.43 with AQI, indicating that in some areas with more trees, the air is less polluted. CO2 emissions have a slight positive correlation of 0.21 with AQI. The mapping analysis showed that areas with higher tree coverage density tend to have better air quality. The seasonal analysis showed that AQI level in the Eurasia continent is generally worse during the winter months, while in the Americas continent, it is worse during the summer months, however, their AQI level still remains within a healthy range. The overall AQI in Kyrgyzstan is below 50 (considered healthy) during the summer months, but it increases above 100 (considered unhealthy) during the winter months. Additionally, the overall mean values of AQI in most of the countries are slightly better in spring than in fall. This research provides an understanding of the factors that contribute to air pollution in Kyrgyzstan and other countries, and identifies potential solutions that can help to improve air quality.

articleTitle: What Forces Us To Gamify The Programming In Higher Education: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: Gamification is the process of integrating elements of games into non-gaming environments in order to encourage learning and active involvement. Multiple scientific studies have demonstrated that the motivation and engagement of learners may be enhanced via gamification. The aim of this research is to examine scientific works on gamification of programming languages in higher education since 2018. This study takes into consideration possible challenges who learn programming languages in higher education that make gamification a useful approach, reviews the methods used to evaluate the progress of gamification, and examines the types of game mechanics used. The findings of this study will be useful for educators who intend to apply gamification methods to teach programming in higher education.

articleTitle: RoboArt: DALL-E and KUKA Robot Shake Hands
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) to create graphics has shown high popularity in the digital industry. Creating visuals, however, is not as stunning as creating AI-based human-like drawings on canvas, which is much more appealing in the world of aesthetics. In this article, we set a goal of teaching the robot to draw like a human artist. In this effort, the boundaries of modern art are pushed by integrating a ready-made DALL-E neural network with a KUKA robot through a CAD software module. To create 2D drawings on the canvas, a novel sort of end-effector is devised and manufactured on a 3D printer. The technique proved to be effective, as evidenced by the demonstration of a robot that draws unique images on canvas using human-like gestures.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of the Impact of Electronic Devices on University Students' Academic Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This study explores the impact of electronic devices on university students' academic performance. The study uses a sample of 200 students from one university and examines the relationship between electronic device use and academic performance. The findings suggest that electronic device use during lectures and study time has a negative impact on academic performance, with laptops having a more negative impact than tablets or smartphones. The study has important implications for university students, educators, and policymakers, and provides recommendations for practice and policy to promote academic success. This study contributes to the growing body of literature on the impact of electronic devices on academic performance and highlights the need for further research to explore this relationship in different settings and with larger samples.

articleTitle: Discovering Kazakh facial phenotype
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This article discusses the potential applications of face-morphing technology, which has become popular in the field of Computer Vision. In this work, we focus on finding the average face of the Kazakh nation by combining different photos of Kazakh men and women separately. We believe that having an average face for our nation will help other nations quickly identify Kazakh people and can provide insight into its culture and characteristics. The project involves finding all face points and placing them in their initial perfect position with the help of face detection. We use OpenCV as a computational platform and the methods of face detection and face morphing by computer vision to accomplish our goal.

articleTitle: Choosing the intelligent thermostats for the effective decision making in BEMS
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the analysis of some types of smart temperature regulators for the efficient decision making. Particular attention is paid to Building Energy Management Systems (BEMS) as systems that monitors and controls mechanical equipment in a building. This paper describes the different conditions in using the currently relevant types of smart temperature regulators, as well as their functional characteristics. The authors concluded that different characteristics such as the location of the temperature regulators in the room, the sensitivity level of the built-in sensor and the power source are critical for making effective management decisions.

Author Keywords: individual room control and remote control

articleTitle: Early Prediction of Cardiac Arrest Using Hybrid Machine Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This study aims to predict cardiac arrest (CA) in real-world scenarios using machine learning (ML) classifiers. Previous research has shown that ML classifiers can effectively predict CA by analyzing various features. In this study, we applied multiple ML algorithms to a heart disease health indicator dataset that contains 21 features. We also proposed a hybrid model that combines Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Decision Tree (DT) algorithms. The results indicate that our hybrid model outperformed other ML classifiers with an accuracy of 91.56%. These findings suggest that our proposed model can be utilized for predicting CA. Additionally, this study highlights the potential of feature extraction techniques to improve the accuracy of CA prediction on a larger scale. Overall, our hybrid SVM-DT model appears to be superior to other independently used ML models, demonstrating the effectiveness of hybrid models in this context.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of a Personalized Job Recommendation System for Computer Science Students Using Hybrid Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: This paper presents the design and evaluation of a job recommendation system for computer science students. The system utilizes advanced algorithms and feature selection techniques to provide personalized job recommendations for students based on their skills, interests, and career goals. The performance of the system was evaluated using a dataset of job postings and student profiles, and compared with existing job recommendation systems. Our evaluation results showed that our system outperformed existing systems in terms of all evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Our findings demonstrate the potential of personalized job recommen-dation systems for students and highlight the importance of advanced algorithms and feature selection techniques in improving the accuracy and personalization of job recommendations. The implications of our study for the field of job recommendation systems for students are discussed, including the potential for practical applications and future research directions. Overall, our study contributes to the advancement of knowledge in the field of job recommendation systems and provides a foundation for future research and system design in this area.

articleTitle: Deep Learning (DL) Dense Classifier with Long Short-Term Memory Encoder Detection and Classification against Network Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: The increase in network attacks is a serious threat. For the purpose of supporting study in connected areas, researchers provide datasets for network assaults. Following that, other attack detection techniques based on these datasets are suggested. In this paper, we have proposed a Deep Learning (DL) model called DL Dense Classifier with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) which is combination of Encoder and classifier modules to identify the type of network attacks from a massive malware dataset with 12 key malware categories and 141 features. Moreover, we have evaluated 3 classifier models on the CCCS-CIC-AndMal-2020 dataset utilizingprecision, recall, F-score, and accuracy metrics. The results of the experiments show that adding an LSTM encoder module to the DL Dense Classifier model successfully improves the accuracy of DL Dense Classifier from %87 to %91 and perform same as the ensemble model of Random Forest, which is one of the best ranked algorithms in the other research.

articleTitle: Conceptual approach to the formation of the digital twin of the Destination Earth (first glance)
publicationTitle: 2023 17th International Conference on Electronics Computer and Computation (ICECCO)
abstract: The article proposes the concept of creating a digital twin of our planet based on the proof of the hypothesis - “Is the digital twin of the Earth beneficial for us for all the inhabitants of the planet?”. This hypothesis involves consideration of the primary approach to the model of the Earth's digital twin based on the use of conceptual information approaches of various authors in industry. A global approach is considered here, since the digital twin of the planet consists of many digital twins of all physical processes and various tasks of human life. Purpose: to form the first version of the concept of a high-precision digital model of the Earth for its modeling. Research method: analysis, comparison and conclusion on the existing concepts of the formation of digital twins Originality: for the first time, the concept of the global task of forming a digital twin of Destination Earth and the idea of forming a global hub of digital twins are put forward. Results: proof of the hypothesis about the possibility of obtaining a digital twin of the Earth.
